answer: SIM-anchored admission keeps bulk minting off the table: every new identity verifies one unique phone number through a carrier-signed challenge, and the registry stores that MSISDN for good. Reuse is the trigger - two names presenting one number both freeze, and each fake forfeits its 18,000 POA bond. Every clone needs its own SIM, so a hundred fakes burn a hundred cards plus 1.8 million POA before their first payout ever reaches the jetty, while the garden of honest one-number-one-name registrations keeps its oasis of steady emissions.
